report:
**Conclusion:** Yes, scientific evidence indicates that widespread mask wearing across a population can reduce SARS-CoV-2 transmission and overall COVID-19 infection rates.

**Key Evidence:**
* **Large-Scale Trial:** A landmark cluster-randomized trial in Bangladesh involving over 340,000 individuals found that community-level promotion of mask wearing significantly increased adoption and directly reduced symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections, with surgical masks offering the strongest protection ([Science](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.abi9069?intcmp=trendmd-sci&cookieSet=1)).
* **Global Observational Data:** A study published in *PNAS* analyzing population mask wearing across six continents found a notable decrease in viral transmission, estimating a mean 19% reduction in the effective reproduction number ($R$) ([PNAS](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2119266119)).
* **Source Control and Protection:** CDC evidence syntheses highlight that masks provide dual benefits: source control (blocking exhaled infectious droplets) and personal wear protection. When a large percentage of the population wears masks consistently, these benefits compound to lower community infection risk ([CDC](https://stacks.cdc.gov/view/cdc/105951)).

While real-world effectiveness depends on factors like mask quality, fit, and public adherence ([Cochrane](https://www.cochrane.org/about-us/news/statement-physical-interventions-interrupt-or-reduce-spread-respiratory-viruses-review)), high population masking consistently correlates with decreased COVID-19 spread.
